decision_authority.policy: MRX continuous quality-gated publication and two-image article creative directive

title: How Much Are Mineral Rights Worth: Checklist Without Obligation
findings: Complete current MDX SHA-256 is 3abfe9593b5074dee5c50fb250a626185aeffd6b964334bfe6f7ce8431c4be8f; all 6 declared official sources passed live access review.

MRX price, scope, methodology, commercial-role, privacy, and communication-choice claims remain bounded to current first-party pages; FTC concepts remain bounded to general truth-in-advertising and clear-disclosure guidance without a legal compliance conclusion.

The article uses no fabricated owners, agreements, documents, communications, fees, deposits, cards, offers, prices, deadlines, testimonials, or owner-specific title, legal, tax, privacy, communications-law, accounting, engineering, investment, or valuation conclusions.

sources_inspected.label: Mineral Rights Xchange, Homepage Review Disclosures (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current MRX homepage describes a free and confidential directional underwriter review with no obligation and no pressure, while its footer limits the material to general educational information rather than certified professional advice.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses those first-party statements only to identify the advertised review boundary and educational scope; it does not treat them as a legal compliance determination, universal privacy promise, guaranteed response time, promised value, offer, or transaction outcome.

sources_inspected.label: Mineral Rights Xchange, Published DCF Methodology (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current MRX methodology describes the free review as requiring no card and no obligation and identifies its output as a directional underwriter range with stated assumptions rather than a regulated valuation certification, title opinion, reserve certification, legal or tax opinion, or guarantee.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the methodology only to identify the price, deliverable, assumptions, limits, and stopping boundary an owner should confirm; it does not turn the review into a professional assignment, guaranteed value, offer, or recommendation to transact.

sources_inspected.label: Mineral Rights Xchange, Terms of Use and AI Disclosure (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current MRX terms describe the website and AI assistant as educational, require users to upload only files they are authorized to share, separate requested-call scheduling from consent to marketing texts, and state that MRX may be a buyer with that relationship disclosed in writing before an agreement is signed.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses those terms to distinguish a review request, document-sharing authorization, communication choices, commercial-role disclosure, and any later transaction agreement; it does not interpret the terms for an owner or announce that a particular practice or agreement complies with law.

sources_inspected.label: Mineral Rights Xchange, Privacy Policy (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current MRX privacy policy describes categories of information collected, purposes, sharing, security, retention, and user choices.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article cites that page only as the current first-party place to review data-handling terms and choices before sharing documents; it does not promise anonymity, perfect security, universal confidentiality, deletion timing, or legal compliance.

sources_inspected.label: Mineral Rights Xchange, Communication Preferences (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current MRX communication-preferences page provides a first-party route for users to review or change available communication choices.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article identifies that route as a practical preference-management checkpoint only; it does not give communications-law advice, promise that every channel or message is covered, or determine the legal effect of a particular choice.

sources_inspected.label: Federal Trade Commission, Advertising FAQs for Small Business (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Federal Trade Commission small-business advertising FAQ describes general principles that advertising should be truthful and non-deceptive, supported by evidence, and clear and conspicuous about material qualifications, including conditions attached to free claims.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses that federal guidance only as a general transparency principle for clearly defining free and no-obligation claims; it does not offer consumer-protection legal advice or conclude that MRX or another party complies with any law.
